title: GD&T for machinists: the 14 symbols and when each one matters
summary: An inventory of the fourteen common GD&T geometric characteristic symbols with shop-floor cues for when each one changes how you make or inspect a part.

blocks.title: Fourteen symbols, and when they change your setup
blocks.body: GD&T is not decoration on a print. Each geometric characteristic tells you what relationship must be true — and therefore what to datum, what to measure, and what not to over-constrain. This page inventories the usual fourteen and tags when each one matters on a machine.

items.label: Groups: form, profile, orientation, location, runout
Most controls are meaningless without a frame

nodes.title: Form (no datum)
nodes.detail: Straightness, flatness, circularity, cylindricity — the feature vs itself.

nodes.title: Profile
nodes.detail: Profile of a line / surface — often datum-referenced for real parts.

nodes.title: Orientation
nodes.detail: Angularity, perpendicularity, parallelism — attitude to a datum.

nodes.title: Location
nodes.detail: Position, concentricity, symmetry — where the feature sits (position rules modern shops).

nodes.title: Runout
nodes.detail: Circular and total runout — spinning functional control.

blocks.heading: Form controls
columns: When it matters on the machine
rows: Shafts, knife edges, extrusions — controls bend without saying where it sits
Sealing faces, plate tops — how planar, not how parallel to something else
Seal diameters, bearing seats in cross-section — every slice round
Pins and bores as a 3D cylinder — round + straight + taper together
blocks.caption: Form callouts do not use datums. They still eat time if the tolerance is tighter than your process naturally holds.

blocks.heading: Profile controls
rows: 2D curves on a section — cams, airfoils in a plane
3D freeform / contoured faces — molds, aero, fairing surfaces
blocks.caption: With datums, profile becomes a powerful all-in-one location+form control. Without, it is mostly form.

blocks.heading: Orientation controls
rows: Any non-90° relationship to a datum — wedges, dovetails
Bores square to faces, shoulders square to axes — square setups
Opposite faces, slots, rails — keep mates even
blocks.caption: Orientation assumes a datum reference frame. Clock your vise and indicators to those datums.

blocks.heading: Location controls
rows: Hole patterns, pins, slots — the modern default for 'where is this feature'
Rare on new prints; median-point control — ask before over-inspecting
Also uncommon now; center-plane equality — position often replaces it
blocks.caption: If a new print says concentricity/symmetry, clarify with engineering. Position + runout usually carry function today.

blocks.heading: Runout controls
rows: Each circular element while rotating about a datum axis — shafts, seals
Entire surface as it spins — stricter functional spin control
blocks.caption: Runout is how the part behaves when it turns. Indicate it the way it runs in service when you can.

items.label: No datum on the feature control frame → form (or undatumed profile)
items.detail: You are fighting process capability, not fixture alignment.

items.label: Perpendicularity / parallelism / angularity → lock datums before cutting
items.detail: Indicate the datum surfaces the print names, not the ones that are convenient.

items.label: Position on a pattern → true position math / functional gage thinking
items.detail: Do not invent a ± coordinate story that the print did not ask for.

items.label: Runout → spin about the datum axis the print shows
items.detail: Centers, V-blocks, or a functional spindle — match the callout.

blocks.title: Modifiers you will also see
blocks.body: Ⓟ (projected), Ⓜ (MMC), Ⓛ (LMC), and datum references A|B|C change bonus tolerance and inspection. This inventory is the fourteen characteristics — modifiers deserve their own page when you are ready.

blocks.heading: Which control?
blocks.prompt: A bearing bore must stay round and straight along its length as one cylinder, with no datum. Which characteristic fits best?
blocks.explanation: Cylindricity is the no-datum form control for a cylindrical surface as a whole. Runout needs a datum axis; position locates a feature.

blocks.heading: Use it on the next print
blocks.body: Circle every feature control frame. Name the group (form / profile / orientation / location / runout). Then decide datums and inspection before you touch the machine.
